name: ROUNDDOWN
description: ROUNDDOWN rounds a number down to a specified number of decimal places, always toward zero.
tldr: ROUNDDOWN always rounds numbers down, never up, to the specified decimal places.

parameters.name: num_digits
parameters.description: The number of decimal places to round to.

basicExample.description: Always round down to 2 decimal places
basicExample.explanation: Rounds 3.14999 down to 2 decimal places, resulting in 3.14.

advancedExamples.title: Round down to nearest 1000
advancedExamples.description: Round down to the nearest thousand for budget estimation
advancedExamples.explanation: 5999 becomes 5000 when rounded down to the nearest thousand.

howItWorks: ROUNDDOWN always rounds numbers toward zero, effectively truncating decimal values. 1.999 rounded to 0 decimal places becomes 1.

howToSteps.name: Select output cell
howToSteps.text: Choose where the result should appear.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The result shows the rounded-down number.

limitations: ROUNDDOWN always decreases the number (or makes it more negative).
Use ROUNDUP for the opposite behavior.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ROUNDDOWN works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What is the difference between ROUNDDOWN and INT?
faq.answer: INT rounds negative numbers away from zero, while ROUNDDOWN always rounds toward zero. INT(-1.5) = -2, ROUNDDOWN(-1.5, 0) = -1.
